---
title: "KRW's race and gender report cards"
subtitle: "5.3 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Figures 7, 10A and 14"
description: "Marginal summaries and pairwise statements in the archived cards for 97 firms."
---

KRW's report cards state directions between grades and withhold comparisons within grades. Grade 1 denotes the end
with the highest oriented target. Race and signed gender gaps have separate target definitions and pairwise
posterior probabilities. The cards display firm-level means and intervals together with the error probabilities of
stated comparisons. A correct direction receives reward λ, a wrong direction costs 1 and withholding has payoff 0;
λ .25 corresponds to τ .20. The discordance rate DR divides the expected wrong count by all 4,656 unordered pairs,
whereas E/N uses only stated pairs.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Published race card.** The card states 1,324 of 4,656 pairs, with expected wrong share E/N .136.
  Its risk .1818 splits into .0387 for errors and .1431 for withholding. The full firm display and between-grade table show that directions between distant grades are more reliable than adjacent ones here.
- **Reveal grade 1.** Grades can be displayed sequentially. The remaining bands stay in place; unrevealed firms are
  omitted from the disclosure and between-grade tables until those grades are displayed.
- **Sort by estimate.** State Farm moves 69 rows inside its grade. Changing the row order changes no reported
  direction. Genuine Parts and AutoNation illustrate why estimates alone do not determine the card.
- **λ .08: first race split.** The risk .07406 is slightly below all withheld, .07407. The extra decimal
  prevents rounding from hiding that distinction. The displayed card is still an archived KRW grid card.
- **Published gender card.** It states 731 pairs. Both ends of its signed scale are contact gaps; three stated
  directions are more likely wrong than right. The note identifies these firms and probabilities.
- **One grade.** Nothing is stated. E/N is NA: no disclosure, meaning undefined; the app draws no E/N bar.

The precision view plots each firm’s original sampling SE against its current grade, with a complete named table.
KRW’s prior depends on precision; uncertain firms sharing the middle grade is not evidence of average behavior.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Grid cards were computed with KRW’s code under archived probabilities and solver tolerances. Their evaluations
here use the released postrank probabilities and supply no new optimality certificate. Race’s baseline card is
Figure 7; gender is Figure 14 (§VIII). Figures 5A and 6 are in §V.E, and Figure 10A is in §VI.B.
